transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here. What brings you into the clinic today?

My mind just won’t shut off about work and everything else, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off no matter what I do. A friend suggested I should talk to a professional, so I decided to finally come in.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worry, and did it start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

It's been going on for about nine months now, starting right around the time I got promoted at work. I took on a lot of heavy new responsibilities, like being the primary bilingual contact for a major corporate client and mentoring new hires, and it quickly felt like I could never truly disconnect.
Along with the constant worry, have you also been experiencing a persistently low mood, sadness, or a loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

I wouldn't say I feel deeply sad or down, but I have been skipping things I normally love, like my weekly dance nights and hiking. I've been canceling plans with friends mostly because I feel completely drained, exhausted, and just too anxious to keep up with anything outside of work.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms alongside this worry, such as muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or feeling constantly restless and on edge?

Yes, definitely. I feel constantly wired and on edge, like I've had way too much coffee, and I'm always clenching my shoulders or tapping my foot. My sleep is also terrible; I lie awake until 2 a.m. replaying work scenarios and wake up feeling like I never actually rested.
Are your worries mostly focused on your work and new responsibilities, or do you find yourself excessively worrying about other everyday things, like family, health, or minor daily tasks?

It definitely goes beyond just work. My brain constantly runs worst-case scenarios about all sorts of things, like my parents' health, my student loans, or saying something stupid while mentoring. It feels like there's always some disaster I'm about to cause or miss.
To help me get a complete picture, are you currently taking any medications, consuming a lot of caffeine, or do you have any known medical conditions like thyroid issues?

I'm not currently taking any medications, and I don't have any medical conditions like thyroid issues. I also don't actually drink much caffeine at all, even though I constantly feel wired and on edge as if I've had way too much of it.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of pervasive, uncontrollable worry about multiple everyday topics (work, family health, finances), accompanied by physical symptoms of motor tension (muscle tightness, restlessness), sleep disturbance, and feeling constantly on edge for a duration of 9 months, in the absence of organic causes (such as thyroid dysfunction or excessive caffeine), strongly support a diagnosis of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). No other primary psychiatric conditions are indicated, so we can finalize the diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple everyday domains (work responsibilities, parents' health, student loans, and social interactions) persisting for 9 months, which meets the 6-month duration criterion for Generalized Anxiety Disorder. This worry is accompanied by several somatic and cognitive symptoms, including muscle tension, sleep disturbance, fatigue, and feeling constantly on edge. These symptoms cause significant functional impairment (social withdrawal, skipping hobbies) and are not attributable to substance use (low caffeine intake, no medications) or a general medical condition (no thyroid issues).
